# Results — Study 596 (Bond Tent / Rising Equity Glidepath)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Kitces & Pfau 2014) — **hold more bonds on the day you retire and re-raise equity through
retirement (a "rising equity glidepath", the back half of the "bond tent") to cut
sequence-of-returns risk** — tested on 30-year retirement cohorts with 4% real withdrawals on
the Shiller 1871+ real-return tape. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-07-03** (run date); the
cached Shiller extract's last **complete full-data month is 2023-06** — no partial months are
used. Fingerprint `7246f42140ba`. Cousin of studies [172](../../172-hundred-minus-age/) (the
100-minus-age accumulation glidepath) and [173](../../173-four-percent-rule/) (the 4% rule
itself); what is new here is the **glidepath SHAPE in retirement** and its decomposition.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | Shiller S&P 500 monthly (GitHub raw mirror, cache-first `_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`) |
| Window | 1871-02 → 2023-06 (**1,829 months**); real EQ total return **+6.90%/yr**, real BD **+2.39%/yr** (realised equity premium **4.52 pp**) |
| Bond leg | 10-year Treasury first-order approx (carry − 7 × Δy), **CPI-deflated** — a deliberate decision: both legs real, unlike nominal-bond variants; stated, not hidden |
| Cohorts | **1,470** monthly-start 30-year retirements (1871-02 → 1993-07), annual withdrawals at the start of each year, annual rebalance to the year's target weight |
| Strategies | static **60/40**, **50/50**, **40/60**; **rising** tent 30%→70% equity (avg 50%); **declining** mirror 70%→30% (avg 50%) |
| Execution / costs | year-*j* weights are a deterministic function of years-since-retirement, fixed at retirement and set at the end of year *j−1* (one clean lag — no information beyond the calendar); **10 bps one-way × traded value** (withdrawal sales + rebalance turnover) |

> **No survivorship:** the tape is a single index series, not a survivor panel. The relevant
> bias is the opposite one and is named below: the US is the **best-performing equity market in
> recorded history**, which flatters *every* equity-heavy rule — and, as the decomposition
> shows, it is precisely what kills the tent.

## Success rates — the tent trails everywhere

Share of the 1,470 cohorts never depleted over 30 years, by real withdrawal rate:

| wr | 60/40 | 50/50 | 40/60 | **rising tent** | declining mirror |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 4.0% | **96.33%** | 95.85% | 93.81% | **94.01%** | 95.85% |
| 4.5% | **88.71%** | 85.17% | 77.82% | **79.86%** | 86.05% |
| 5.0% | **75.78%** | 69.80% | 59.86% | **60.41%** | 73.95% |
| 5.5% | **63.40%** | 57.21% | 51.84% | **52.65%** | 62.65% |

Terminal real wealth at the 4% rule (multiple of initial):

| strategy | mean | median | p05 | failures |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 60/40 | **1.880** | 1.332 | 0.146 | 54/1470 |
| 50/50 | 1.555 | 0.985 | 0.041 | 61/1470 |
| 40/60 | 1.260 | 0.698 | 0.000 | 91/1470 |
| **rising tent** | 1.465 | 0.824 | **0.000** | **88/1470** |
| declining mirror | 1.624 | 1.115 | 0.095 | 61/1470 |

SAFEMAX (highest wr surviving *every* cohort): 60/40 **3.68%** · declining **3.62%** · 50/50
**3.61%** · rising **3.57%** · 40/60 3.53%. Even the all-cohort floor ranks the tent below the
static benchmark *and below its own mirror image*. (SAFEMAX sits below study 173's 4.14%
because our bond leg is a **CPI-deflated 10-year** — crushed in the 1940s–70s — our cohorts are
monthly-start, and we charge 10 bps; the data decision is stated above.)

## The decomposition — the third axis IS the myth-check

Identity: `rising − 60/40 = (rising − 50/50) + (50/50 − 60/40)` — shape at matched average
equity, plus just-holding-less-equity. HAC *t* = Newey-West on per-cohort terminal-wealth
differences at 4%, bandwidth forced to the **full 360-month overlap**; block-bootstrap 95% CIs
(1,000 reps, circular 120-month blocks on the joint monthly tape, seed 596 — blocks preserve
within-decade dynamics, destroy cross-decade mean reversion; stated, not hidden).

| comparison | mean ΔTW @4% | HAC *t* | bootstrap 95% CI (ΔTW) | Δsuccess @4% | Δsuccess @5% | boot CI Δsucc@5% |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **HEADLINE** rising − 60/40 | **−0.415** | **−6.11** | [−1.429, −0.192] | −2.31 pp | **−15.37 pp** | [−20.00, +1.36] |
| **SHAPE** rising − 50/50 (matched avg) | −0.090 | −1.85 | [−0.328, −0.024] | −1.84 pp | −9.39 pp | [−11.43, +1.23] |
| **TIMING** rising − declining (mirror) | −0.159 | −1.53 | [−0.619, −0.035] | −1.84 pp | −13.54 pp | [−17.96, +3.13] |
| **ALLOCATION** 50/50 − 60/40 | −0.325 | −5.92 | [−1.126, −0.128] | −0.48 pp | −5.99 pp | [−8.91, +0.55] |

Reading: the tent's shortfall vs 60/40 is decisively real (HAC *t* = **−6.11**, bootstrap CI
excludes 0). Both components point the **wrong way for the claim**: holding less equity is a
certified cost (*t* = −5.92), and the *shape itself* — the only new thing the tent adds — is
negative at matched average equity (*t* = −1.85, bootstrap mean-ΔTW CI excludes 0) and loses
the pure-timing race against its own mirror image. Nowhere does the tape produce the claimed
*benefit*; there is **no positive effect to certify** at any threshold.

## The advertised sweet spot fails too — high-CAPE retirements

The tent is pitched hardest for retirements at expensive valuations. Within the **338
top-quartile PE10** cohorts, success rates:

| wr | 60/40 | 50/50 | **rising tent** | declining |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 4.0% | **84.0%** | 82.0% | 74.3% | 82.0% |
| 4.5% | **58.6%** | 50.3% | 39.6% | 51.8% |
| 5.0% | **35.8%** | 30.5% | 27.2% | 31.7% |

## Where the folklore comes from — 1929 vs 1966

Terminal real wealth at 4%, famous cohorts: retiring **1929-09** (deflationary crash — bonds
hold value): rising **1.251** vs 60/40 0.390, declining **0.000** — the tent does *exactly* its
job. Retiring **1966-01** (long stagflation): **everything fails** (all five strategies 0.000);
retiring **1972-12**: rising 0.240 vs 60/40 0.223 — a rounding-error rescue. Of the **54**
cohorts that fail 60/40 at 4% (all starting 1964–1969), the tent rescues **5.6%** of them; its
own failure band is *wider* (starts 1961–1969, 88 failures). The tent insures against a short,
sharp, deflationary crash — the tape's dominant retirement killer was a **15-year inflation
grind that destroyed bonds too**, and the tent walks equity *up* into the recovery it just
missed while holding bonds through their worst decade.

## Robustness — every tent shape, every cost level

| variant | succ @4% | succ @5% | mean TW @4% | HAC *t* vs 60/40 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| rising 30→70 (headline) | 94.01% | 60.41% | 1.465 | −6.11 |
| rising 30→60 (Kitces-Pfau) | 93.61% | 58.64% | 1.338 | −6.75 |
| rising 30→70 by yr 15 (fast) | 95.71% | 68.84% | 1.752 | −2.25 |
| rising 20→80 (deep tent) | 93.47% | 57.21% | 1.411 | −5.67 |

Every variant trails 60/40; the *faster* the tent exits bonds, the less it loses. Costs are a
non-factor: at 0 / 10 / 25 bps one-way, 60/40 success @4% is 96.33 / 96.33 / 96.26% and rising
94.01 / 94.01 / 93.95%.

## Synthetic control — the engine is faithful, and it explains the literature

20 independent seeded worlds per setting; detector = rising vs declining (same 50% average
equity — pure timing), one-sample *t* across worlds. *(Machinery proof only — never cited as
market evidence.)*

| world | Δsuccess (pp) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **EXACT NULL** — no withdrawals, i.i.d. (mirror schedules are exchangeable) | +0.00 (Δp05 −0.031) | n/a (*t* = −1.05 on Δp05) |
| **TENT WORLD** — wr 4%, i.i.d., equity premium **0 pp** | **+5.99** | **+5.65** |
| wr 4%, premium 2 pp | +4.50 | +4.02 |
| wr 4%, premium **4.5 pp (historical)** | +2.54 | +2.92 |
| wr 5%, premium 4.5 pp (historical) | **−3.86** | −3.43 |

The engine finds nothing at the exact null and lights up when the tent's benefit truly exists —
so the real-tape verdict is not a construction artefact. And the sweep explains the literature:
in an **i.i.d. Monte Carlo** world (Kitces-Pfau's laboratory) the tent genuinely helps at a 4%
withdrawal rate, shrinking as the equity premium grows and flipping sign at higher withdrawal
rates. The *real* tape is harsher than i.i.d.: its worst sequences are decade-plus inflation
regimes that crush bonds simultaneously — the one structure a bond tent cannot survive and that
Monte Carlo, by construction, never generates.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed benefit does not exist on 152 years of US tape: the rising
  tent trails static 60/40 on **every** metric (success at every withdrawal rate, mean/median/
  p05 terminal wealth, SAFEMAX), and the shortfall is decisively certified (HAC *t* = **−6.11**,
  bootstrap CI excludes 0). The decomposition kills both channels: less-equity is a certified
  cost (*t* = −5.92) and the shape itself loses at matched average equity (*t* = −1.85) — the
  tent even loses to its own **mirror image** (declining 70→30). Robust across four tent
  shapes, costs 0–25 bps, and the high-CAPE "sweet spot". Named caveat: the US tape is the
  best equity market in history (flattering equity-heavy rules), and our bond leg is a
  CPI-deflated 10-year (harsh on bonds in 1940–80) — both stated as decisions.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no benefit to deploy: adopting the tent historically cost
  **−0.42×** terminal wealth and **−2.3 pp** success at 4% (−15.4 pp at 5%) vs a plain
  two-ETF 60/40 that is strictly simpler to run. Perfectly implementable — and implementing it
  buys you less safety, not more.
- **Third axis — "Is the tent's benefit sequence-risk timing, or just holding less equity?" —
  BUSTED (neither).** On the tape the timing channel is *negative* (loses the mirror race) and
  the less-equity channel is a certified cost. The advertised mechanism only exists in i.i.d.
  Monte Carlo with a low equity premium at a moderate withdrawal rate — the synthetic sweep
  reproduces Kitces-Pfau there (+6 pp, *t* +5.7 at 0 premium) — but 152 years of US history,
  with its long inflation regimes that break bonds and stocks together, never paid it.
